newsitem.title: UK: UK Trades Union Congress to meet BA unions.
newsitem.headline: UK Trades Union Congress to meet BA unions.

text.p: The UK Trades Union Congress (TUC) said on Tuesday its general secretary, John Monks, had invited representatives of British Airways Plc unions to meet him to discuss the current disputes with the airline and consider support for them.
BA faces strike threats from cabin crew in a long-running pay dispute and from ground staff in a separate row over BA's plans to sell off its catering division.

The company has said it believes there is no difficulty in resolving the ground staff issue, but maintains a hostile stance to the cabin crew in what is the first major industrial dispute since the Labour government took power last month.
Bill Morris, general secretary of the main union involved, the Transport and General Workers Union, said earlier on Wednesday that BA was trying to pick off the cabin crew against the ground staff.
The TUC said Monks had invited the TGWU, general union GMB, as well as engineering union AEEU, white collar union MSF and the pilots' union BALPA to meet him at 1430 GMT.

"The meeting will hear reports from the TGWU and the GMB about their disputes with British Airways and will consider support for their efforts to secure a negotiated settlement with BA," the TUC said in a statement.
